subject: CorpZen - SSO/SCIM/IP & service-account cutover coordination
messages:
From: Spencer Hale <spencer@corpzen.com>
To: jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Kickoff: CorpZen Redwood access - SSO/SCIM/IP cutover & service accounts

Hi Jonas/Monica,

Thanks for onboarding Redwood. We'd like to kick off the access-coordination for CorpZen's production cutover this quarter. High-level asks:
- SSO with our IdP (SAML 2.0) and SCIM provisioning for user and group sync
- IP egress allowlist for API calls from our VPC
- Scoped service accounts for automation and CI (least-privilege)
- Org policies around invitation domains, role defaults, and session length

We are targeting a go-live window Sept 15-22. Could you share a recommended cutover cadence and what we need to prepare on our side (IdP metadata, SCIM attribute mapping, network egress IPs, required service account roles)?

Attaching our IdP metadata and a CSV of current egress IP ranges for your reference.

Thanks,
Spencer Hale
Head of Infra - CorpZen
spencer@corpzen.com

Attachments: CorpZen-IdP-metadata.xml, CorpZen-egress-ips.csv

From: jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Spencer Hale <spencer@corpzen.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 13:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: CorpZen Redwood access - SSO/SCIM/IP cutover & service accounts

Hi Spencer — great to meet you and thanks for the artifacts.

High-level approach we recommend: a three-phase cutover with clear fallbacks. Short summary below; attached is a 1-page cutover playbook PDF with timelines and owner notes.

Phase A (Prep, 3-5 business days)
- Exchange IdP SAML metadata and verify ACS/Entity IDs.
- SCIM: agree attribute mapping for username, email, groups, and an external_id field. We prefer using external_id for cross-system reconciliation.
- Service accounts: define two named service accounts (deploy-runner@corpzen, metrics-ingest@corpzen) with scoped roles. We will provide a minimal role template.
- IP allowlist: please confirm stable egress ranges; we will create environment blocks for staging/prod.

Phase B (Staging validation, 2 business days)
- Configure SAML in staging, enable SCIM in dry-run (provision only to group X).
- Smoke tests for login, group sync, and API access using service accounts.

Phase C (Cutover & monitoring, 1 business day + 3-day watch)
- Switch SAML to production, enable SCIM provisioning, and flip traffic to new service accounts.
- 72-hour watch with daily checkpoint calls and rollback plan in play.

Open questions for your team (please reply inline):
1) Preferred SAML NameID format (email or persistent)?
2) Any SCIM group nesting we should be aware of?
3) Are we allowed to create service accounts scoped to a single tenant/project in your environment, or do you require org-level accounts?

I attached the playbook: CorpZen-cutover-playbook-v1.pdf.

cc Ben to handle SCIM mapping specifics. Monica will coordinate the timeline.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Customer Success - Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: CorpZen Redwood access - SSO/SCIM/IP cutover & service accounts

Thanks Spencer/Jonas — a couple of technical clarifications from the SCIM/roles side so we can prepare templates:

1) SCIM attribute mapping
- We typically map external_id -> corpzen_employee_id, userName -> email, name.givenName/familyName, and groups to an array of local role assignments. If you have an HR id field we can map that to external_id for deterministic updates.

2) Service account scoping
- For the two suggested accounts we recommend:
  a) deploy-runner@corpzen scoped to the single project and token rotation every 90 days
  b) metrics-ingest@corpzen scoped to read-only org metrics with IP-restrictions enforced

3) SAML NameID
- If you can provide email as NameID we avoid mismatches for existing users; persistent NameID requires a stable unique id from your side.

4) Audit/logging
- We will enable tenant-level audit logs; please confirm whether you require export to your SIEM or if Redwood's console retention is sufficient.

If you can reply with preferred NameID format, whether you have an HR id to map, and confirm the intended IPs, I will draft the SCIM mapping JSON and minimal RBAC role templates.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer - Redwood Inference

To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: CorpZen Redwood access - SSO/SCIM/IP cutover & service accounts

Hi Ben/Jonas — quick answers inline below.

1) NameID: we can provide email-based NameID. That would be simplest for us.
2) HR id: yes, employee_id exists and is stable. We can map employee_id -> external_id.
3) Group nesting: we have shallow groups (no deep nesting) but we do have parent-team tags; we can flatten to top-level groups for provisioning.
4) Service accounts: we prefer project-scoped accounts. We will not allow org-level keys for third-party apps.
5) Audit export: we need daily exported audit logs to our SIEM (S3 push) for 90 days.

I attached the IdP metadata and egress IP CSV in my first email, attaching again for convenience.

Thanks,
Spencer

Attachments: CorpZen-IdP-metadata.xml, CorpZen-egress-ips.csv

Thanks Spencer — this is perfect and aligns with our expectations. Action items and owners below; please confirm and we will lock calendar invites.

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Today (Jonas) -> Finalize cutover playbook and share updated timeline (attached v1).
- By EOD Monday (Spencer) -> Confirm IdP metadata (email NameID), provide employee_id field mapping, and confirm final egress IP ranges.
- Tuesday (Ben) -> Deliver SCIM mapping JSON and role templates for the two service accounts.
- Wed (Monica + CorpZen infra) -> Staging config and smoke test window (2 hours).
- Sept 15 (CorpZen prod window) -> Cutover day; Redwood to be on-call 08:00-20:00 ET with 1-hour SLA for rollbacks.

Rollback plan (high level)
- Revert SAML to previous IdP binding for 30 minutes while we triage, or disable provisioning if an undesired SCIM change occurs.

Next steps: Spencer, please reply with the confirmed egress CSV and say yes to the week-of-Sept-15 window. Once confirmed we will send a calendar with a pre-cutover readiness check 48 hours prior.

Thanks all,
Jonas Weber
Customer Success - Redwood Inference
